title: Memento
tagline: A local, screen-free voice assistant that answers a person with Alzheimer's disease from their own memory graph.
problem: People with Alzheimer's disease ask the same orienting questions many times a day: who is coming, where am I, who is this person. Generic assistants do not know their family or routines, and a wrong answer is worse than none.
approach: Caregivers fill a personal knowledge graph (relatives, places, routines, dated memories) stored in Neo4j and indexed in ChromaDB. A spoken question is transcribed by Whisper, the graph and vector stores return the relevant memories with an explainable clinical score, a small local LLM answers from that context only, a grounding guard rejects unsupported names, and Qwen3-TTS speaks the answer.

demo.caption: Three spoken questions from a fictitious patient: the transcript, the memory graph nodes retrieved from Neo4j/ChromaDB, then the spoken answer, with per-stage CPU timings. Rendered from the run recorded by showcase/make_showcase.sh.

limits: CPU-only timings: answer TTS dominates the latency (about 10 s per short sentence).
qwen2.5:0.5b sometimes adds loosely grounded details; the grounding guard tolerates one unknown token, so small slips (a wrong time) can pass.
Demo data is a single fictitious patient; no clinical evaluation has been done.
Live microphone mode and the React runtime are not exercised by the showcase run.
